madison-specs.name: Madison SPECS
sources: published typical fees and CPA coordination
madison-specs.summary: Madison SPECS describes a feasibility analysis, an engineer’s on-site property tour, and a cost segregation report developed in coordination with the client’s CPA.
madison-specs.fit: Owners seeking an on-site study and report coordinated with their existing CPA.
madison-specs.alternative_intro: Madison SPECS alternatives should be compared on the property study you need, not a general tax-planning retainer. Consider AE Tax Advisors for a standalone study with separately scoped tax work, Engineered Tax Services for an engineering-led specialty project, and Maven for detailed engineering with an optional separately priced Form 3115 service.
madison-specs.keep: Madison's published process includes feasibility review, an on-site engineering tour and CPA coordination. Keep it on your shortlist when that workflow fits your building and you want your existing preparer to remain responsible for the return.
madison-specs.boundary: Its report-to-CPA workflow does not establish that every possible support or tax service is bundled. Confirm the specific report, review and support terms.
madison-specs.fee: Madison SPECS' FAQ gives a typical study range of $4,000–$11,000, with each property priced individually using a fixed fee based on size and complexity.
madison-specs.fee_context: This is the provider's general range, not a guaranteed minimum, maximum or quote for your property. Request a proposal identifying inspection, reporting, support and any additional work.
madison-specs.price_status: Published typical study range — property quote required
madison-specs.filing_answer: Madison describes delivering the report to the client's CPA. Identify who prepares any accounting-method change, applies the schedules to the return and handles follow-up questions.
madison-specs.price_comparison: Compare Madison's property-specific engineering quote with AE's $1-per-square-foot study rate and $2,000 minimum. Include the same inspection, schedules, support and preparer handoff. Neither a typical range nor a minimum establishes the total cost for every property.
madison-specs.vs_intro: Compare Madison's engineering-and-CPA coordination workflow with an AE standalone study. Keep any separate advisory or tax-return work outside the study-price comparison until both proposals include the same tasks.
madison-specs.scenario: Suppose you own a multifamily building, have a long-standing CPA and want a study before the next return is prepared. You need the inspection arranged, existing depreciation records reconciled and a report your preparer can review in time.
madison-specs.decision: Consider Madison when its on-site study and CPA-coordination proposal meets those needs. Consider AE when its standalone study scope, published rate and separately quoted implementation fit. Agree on report review and the preparer's responsibilities before engaging either firm.
madison-specs.ae_question: What inspection, report schedules and CPA review support does the AE study include, and what return work is separate?
questions: Does the fixed quote include the on-site visit, engineering work and all report schedules?
Will our CPA review draft findings before the report is finalized?
Who addresses prior depreciation, any Form 3115 work and the final return?
What response period, audit support and additional charges are in the study agreement?
cost_rows: Fixed study fee
Use a quote for the actual building, records and improvement history.
Inspection
Confirm visit arrangements and any travel or access charges.
CPA handoff
Identify report schedules, draft review and accountant-question support.
Tax work and support
Separate filing, method-change preparation and audit-response scope.

engineered-tax-services.name: Engineered Tax Services
engineered-tax-services.summary: Engineered Tax Services lists cost segregation, R&D credits, energy deductions, incentive reports, and 1031 exchange services on its official website.
engineered-tax-services.fit: Owners and CPA teams evaluating engineering-led property studies and separately scoped specialty incentives.
engineered-tax-services.alternative_intro: Alternatives to Engineered Tax Services should match the project you are buying. Compare AE Tax Advisors for a standalone property study, Madison SPECS for an on-site study coordinated with your CPA, and KBKG for professional specialty services or a distinct software workflow.
engineered-tax-services.keep: ETS describes engineering analysis, property inspection, report documentation and coordination with the owner's CPA. Keep it on the shortlist when the proposed engineering and specialty scope matches the property and your professional team.
engineered-tax-services.boundary: A broad specialty menu is not an all-inclusive package. Confirm the particular study and related incentive projects separately.
engineered-tax-services.fee: ETS describes a fixed study fee quoted after an initial benefit analysis. A universal numeric ETS study price was not verified in the official pages reviewed.
engineered-tax-services.fee_context: Request a written property-specific quote. An example study fee or an industry-wide price range is not ETS' tariff or a quote for your building.
engineered-tax-services.filing_answer: ETS describes working with the CPA and delivering a report for return use. Ask who handles each additional schedule, any Form 3115 preparation, return filing and post-delivery question.
engineered-tax-services.price_comparison: Use an actual ETS fixed quote alongside AE's standalone study quote. Add any incentive project, travel, extra buildings, report support and separately contracted tax work to the same scope before comparing totals.
engineered-tax-services.vs_intro: An ETS study and an AE study should be compared as property-specific engagements. Separate engineering deliverables from broader incentives and from the owner's tax planning and filing.
engineered-tax-services.scenario: Suppose you bought a commercial building with recent renovations and your CPA wants engineering schedules before filing. You also want to explore a separate incentive opportunity without assuming it is included in the study.
engineered-tax-services.decision: Consider ETS when the proposed engineering and related specialty work fit the project. Consider AE when its standalone study and separately scoped tax support meet your needs. Ask each firm to identify the report, deadline and responsible professional for every workstream.
engineered-tax-services.ae_question: Which property analysis and report deliverables are in the AE study, and which incentive or tax implementation services need separate scopes?
questions: Which engineering analysis, inspection and cost records does the fixed study quote cover?
Are any energy or other incentive projects separate engagements?
Who reviews findings with the CPA and supplies the return-ready schedules?
What documentation, response support and deadline commitments are included?
cost_rows: Engineering study
Identify buildings, improvements, records and inspection scope.
Specialty projects
Separate any incentive or other tax-service proposal.
Report delivery
Confirm draft review, final schedules and CPA questions.
Implementation
Assign method-change preparation and return work separately where required.

kbkg.name: KBKG
sources: linked CPA Handbook and technical resources
kbkg.summary: KBKG’s website lists specialty work across cost segregation, R&D credits, energy incentives, and fixed-asset reviews. It also offers CostSegregation.com as a separate software workflow.
kbkg.fit: Buyers choosing between professional specialty analysis and a separately scoped software report.
kbkg.alternative_intro: Compare KBKG alternatives after choosing the service category: professional engineering or a software workflow. AE Tax Advisors offers standalone studies; ETS offers engineering-led specialty work; Maven offers detailed studies and a separately priced Form 3115 service. A software starting price cannot stand in for a full-service study quote.
kbkg.keep: Keep KBKG on the shortlist when professional cost segregation, fixed-asset review or a related specialty engagement fits your requirements. Its software route is a distinct purchase that should be evaluated with the preparer who will use the report.
kbkg.boundary: Software and professional services have different scope and eligibility limits. Confirm the current product terms rather than treating a software price as the cost of all KBKG work.
kbkg.fee: KBKG's linked CPA Handbook gives a general fixed-fee study range of $5,000–$15,000 by property size and type. Its separate software page displays a $495 residential report example for $750,000 of tax basis. Obtain a current quote for the selected service.
kbkg.fee_context: The handbook range is general professional-study guidance; the software amount belongs to a separate product and selected property basis. Neither is a universal final price. Confirm inspection, review, support, property limits and preparer fees.
kbkg.price_status: Published professional range and separate software example
kbkg.filing_answer: Identify whether you are purchasing a software report or professional engineering. Confirm who reviews the inputs, handles accountant questions and completes any required filing; a software report is not return preparation.
kbkg.price_comparison: Compare AE's standalone study rate with the matched KBKG professional-study quote. A $495 software report should be compared with other software scope, not represented as KBKG's full-service engineering fee or as the cost of tax implementation.
kbkg.vs_intro: The useful KBKG–AE comparison begins by selecting a professional property study or a software route. Keep the full-service study price separate from software and preparer charges.
kbkg.scenario: Suppose you are comparing a software estimate with an engineering quote for a property with multiple improvements. Your CPA needs to know who verifies the inputs, what documentation supports allocations and who answers questions if the report needs correction.
kbkg.decision: Consider KBKG when its professional or software scope matches the property's needs and the preparer's workflow. Consider AE when a standalone study with an agreed report and support scope fits. Ask for matching deliverables before comparing the amounts.
kbkg.ae_question: How does AE document and review the study inputs and deliver the final schedules, and which professional handles tax implementation?
questions: Is this quote for professional engineering or a software report?
What property limits, inspection, data verification and review apply to this path?
Which supporting schedules and correction or support services are included?
What must the tax preparer do separately, and how is that work priced?
cost_rows: Purchase route
Separate professional-study fees from software pricing.
Property and records
Match the building complexity, improvements and available documentation.
Review and support
Confirm data checks, report corrections and accountant-question coverage.
Preparer services
Add information gathering, method-change analysis and filing where separately required.

cost-segregation-authority.name: Cost Segregation Authority
sources: CSA Partners study services and starting fee
cost-segregation-authority.summary: The current CSA Partners website describes engineering-based cost segregation, property-specific documentation, site verification, audit support, and coordination with CPA and real estate clients.
cost-segregation-authority.fit: Property owners and CPA teams seeking an engineering-based study with documented support.
cost-segregation-authority.alternative_intro: Cost Segregation Authority is presented on its current website as CSA Partners; the site's terms identify Cost Segregation Authority, LLC doing business under that name. Compare alternatives such as AE Tax Advisors, Madison SPECS and Maven on inspection, report documentation, support and CPA handoff.
cost-segregation-authority.keep: CSA Partners describes property-specific engineering work and coordination with CPA clients. Keep it on your shortlist when the proposed scope, support and delivery arrangements meet the property's needs.
cost-segregation-authority.boundary: Confirm the contracting identity and written scope. A public service summary does not establish every tax or support task included in your quote.
cost-segregation-authority.fee: CSA Partners publishes cost segregation studies beginning at $3,000. The final fee varies with property size, complexity, available documentation and engagement scope.
cost-segregation-authority.fee_context: This is a published starting study fee, not an all-inclusive tax advisory or return-preparation package. Request a written quote for the property and any additional work.
cost-segregation-authority.filing_answer: Ask which professional handles the report, accountant questions, any accounting-method change and return preparation. The study agreement should assign each responsibility; do not infer that an unlisted service is unavailable.
cost-segregation-authority.price_comparison: Compare CSA's actual property quote with AE's $1-per-square-foot rate and $2,000 minimum study fee. Depending on area and scope, the resulting amounts can differ in either direction. Match inspection, report and support terms before drawing a cost conclusion.
cost-segregation-authority.vs_intro: Compare CSA Partners' engineering-study proposal with an AE standalone study for the same property. Keep the provider's current identity, support terms and return-preparer responsibilities explicit.
cost-segregation-authority.scenario: Suppose you own several rental buildings and want reports delivered to your CPA ahead of the return deadline. You need separate fees and schedules for each property, a clear inspection plan and a way for your preparer to resolve report questions.
cost-segregation-authority.decision: Consider CSA Partners when its engineering and CPA-coordination scope fits the portfolio. Consider AE when its standalone study quote and separately agreed implementation meet your needs. Ask for property-level schedules and a documented handoff rather than relying on a headline minimum.
cost-segregation-authority.ae_question: Which buildings and report schedules does AE's quote include, and what extra implementation or support work will be priced separately?
questions: Does this quote identify CSA Partners and the exact property scope?
Which inspection, documentation and report schedules are included?
Who handles each CPA question and any method-change or return work?
What are the duration, limits and cost of audit support and other follow-up?
cost_rows: Study minimum
Use the $3,000 starting amount as a reference, then obtain the property quote.
Portfolio scope
List each building, improvement project and required report.
Documentation and handoff
Confirm inspection arrangements, CPA schedules and response responsibilities.
Additional services
Separate return work and any support outside the agreed coverage.

maven-cost-segregation.name: Maven Cost Segregation
maven-cost-segregation.summary: Maven describes detailed engineering studies with physical inspection, CPA coordination and audit support, and separately offers Form 3115 preparation.
maven-cost-segregation.fit: Owners seeking detailed engineering with CPA coordination and optional separately priced method-change preparation.
maven-cost-segregation.alternative_intro: Maven alternatives should be compared on study methodology, inspection, support and any filing package you need. AE Tax Advisors offers standalone studies with separately scoped tax work; Madison SPECS describes an on-site CPA-coordinated process; KBKG offers professional studies and a distinct software route.
maven-cost-segregation.keep: Maven's detailed-study page describes an in-house team, physical inspection, report schedules and CPA coordination. Its separate Form 3115 service is a real offering and should not be described as unavailable.
maven-cost-segregation.boundary: Ask which study and preparation services your quote includes. A study report, Form 3115 preparation and the owner's full tax return are distinct deliverables.
maven-cost-segregation.fee: Maven publishes general detailed-study ranges of $2,500–$4,000 for smaller properties and $5,000–$10,000+ for large or complex properties and portfolios. It separately publishes Form 3115 preparation at $995.
maven-cost-segregation.fee_context: These study ranges are not fixed property quotes. The Form 3115 fee is a separate service; a cost segregation study, if needed, is separately scoped. Confirm records, inspection, preparation, CPA coordination and support in the final proposal.
maven-cost-segregation.price_status: Published study ranges; Form 3115 priced separately
maven-cost-segregation.filing_answer: Maven offers Form 3115 preparation separately and describes coordinating with the CPA. Confirm whether your quote includes that service and who integrates the result into the owner's return.
maven-cost-segregation.price_comparison: Compare Maven's actual study-and-preparation proposal with AE's standalone study and separately quoted tax work. Do not compare a study-only minimum with a quote that also includes Form 3115 preparation or assume either provider includes the full return.
maven-cost-segregation.vs_intro: Maven and AE can be compared for a property study, while any Form 3115 preparation and return work need their own scope. Maven publicly offers that preparation service, so the decision is delivery, coverage and complete cost rather than an assumed missing capability.
maven-cost-segregation.scenario: Suppose you bought a rental several years ago and now want a study while retaining your current CPA. You need existing depreciation reviewed, the study completed and the appropriate implementation route determined and assigned to a professional.
maven-cost-segregation.decision: Consider Maven when its detailed engineering and separately priced preparation match the project. Consider AE when its study and additional tax work can be scoped to your needs. Ask both proposals to assign report delivery, any method-change package and final return integration.
maven-cost-segregation.ae_question: Which report, depreciation review and filing-related tasks will AE accept, and what is the total after separately scoped work?
questions: Which detailed-study range and property scope apply to this quote?
Does the fee include the physical inspection, report schedules and stated audit support?
Is the $995 Form 3115 preparation service needed and included separately?
Who coordinates with the existing CPA and completes the affected tax return?

Match the published range to the building, complexity and property count.
Inspection and schedules

Form 3115
